title: Spatiotemporal-Switchable 2D NIR-II Single-Atom Nanozyme for Single-Cell-Level Surgical Navigation and Glioblastoma Phototherapy
author: Ping Shangguan et al. / Bingyang Shi group, UTS & Harvard
key_claims: 2D single-atom nanozyme platform provides dual-function intraoperative NIR-II imaging (44-micrometer resolution) and postoperative phototherapy for glioblastoma
Platinum atoms catalyze H2O2-to-O2 conversion, countering hypoxic tumor microenvironment; simultaneous photothermal/photodynamic therapy destroys residual microscopic cancer cells
In mouse glioblastoma models: 100% survival at 60 days vs. 42 days for surgery-only controls; no detectable neurological or motor impairments
Targeting molecule enables blood-brain barrier crossing and glioma-specific accumulation
methodology: 2D nanosheet synthesis via semiconductor-adapted atomic placement; NIR-II fluorescent dye conjugation; in vivo mouse glioblastoma xenograft model; survival analysis; histological and behavioral assessment
key_risk: Mouse models only — human translation uncertain. Blood-brain barrier penetration at human scale unproven. Long-term toxicity and immune response not assessed. Scale-up manufacturing of atomically precise 2D sheets is non-trivial.
next_experiment: Primate BBB penetration studies; GLP toxicology; Phase I human trial in recurrent glioblastoma; integrate with C9 physical sensor layer for real-time nanoparticle tracking via NIR-II imaging
notes: Strong translational medicine entry. The 'image then treat' spatiotemporal switching is a concrete realization of active inference (sense → update → act). Connects to C9 physical sensor layer and neuromorphic control loops.
